name: IM-3

surface_window.note: The landing date is known only as 'in 2026', so there is no single window: compare months on the calendar instead.

outcome_note: Will deliver NASA payloads to Reiner Gamma, a lunar swirl, with the Altus-1 data-relay satellite flying alongside (NASA, Aug 2026).

payloads.name: Lunar Vertex
payloads.organisation: Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory
payloads.purpose: Lander and rover suite studying the origin of lunar magnetic fields and swirls.

payloads.name: Cooperative Autonomous Distributed Robotic Exploration
payloads.purpose: Small cooperating rovers with ground-penetrating radar testing autonomous exploration.

payloads.name: MoonLIGHT Pointing Actuator
payloads.purpose: Large reflector for Earth-Moon laser ranging.

payloads.name: Lunar Space Environment Monitor
payloads.organisation: Korea Astronomy and Space Science Institute
payloads.purpose: Detects high-energy charged particles near the surface.

sources.title: NASA Provides Updates on Moon Base Cargo Landers, Tech Demonstrations (Aug 04, 2026)
Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature: Reiner Gamma

notes: NASA's CP-11 page names four NASA payloads; NASA's Aug 2026 update says five. The four named are listed.
The target coordinate is the IAU centre of Reiner Gamma, not a published landing point.

site.name: Reiner Gamma (feature centre)
site.source_note: The IAU centre of Reiner Gamma, used because no landing point is published. It is not a landing point, and numbers here describe the centre of the named feature. No elevation model covers this site: height, slope and terrain are not modelled.

notes: Mission facts are compiled by hand from NASA pages, LROC images and the IAU Gazetteer; every record carries its sources, last read 2026-09-23.
1 of 1 missions have fields no source confirms; they are listed as unconfirmed, never filled in.
Numbers are Sun and Earth geometry at the target over the mission's surface window, not what any lander measured.
1 target(s) lie outside the 80-90 deg S elevation model; there Sun and Earth are computed against a smooth sphere, so terrain could block more.
Where no landing point is published, the target is the IAU centre of the named feature, which is not a landing point.
